edits.value_json: 妈 means “mother” or “mama” in present-day Chinese. A dictionary cites this meaning for traditional 媽; the earliest attestation is unresolved.

The character is also used to address female elders of the mother’s generation, older women, and, in northern usage, servants. The dates of these uses and their relationship to “mother” are unresolved.
An obsolete, isolated “mare; female horse” gloss is reported, but this does not establish a dated occurrence.

The dates and semantic links among the mother and female-address uses are unresolved. The reported obsolete “mare; female horse” gloss has no verified dated occurrence, and its relationship to the mother use is unknown.
女 contributes a female-related meaning in 妈.

馬, written 马 in simplified 妈, is analyzed as the phonetic component. In Zhengzhang Old Chinese, 馬 *mraːʔ and 媽 *maːʔ share an initial and have broadly similar rhymes despite a vowel difference. Modern Mandarin mā and mǎ are a separate comparison and do not prove the historical relationship.
妈 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 媽; 馬 is written 马 in the simplified graph.
妈 means “mother” or “mama.” 女 contributes female-related meaning, while 马 is the simplified form of 馬, the probable sound component.
